title: Unread: the Voynich manuscript
summary: The illustrated book remains undeciphered; its origins, authorship and purpose are still debated. Its text shares some statistical features with natural language but differs in others.
why: A whole illustrated book on early-15th-century vellum, in an unknown script, still defeats every reader.

notes.problem: Source reports both similarities and differences (h2 entropy about 2 vs 3-4 for languages); 'Renaissance Europe' overstates a stylistic 'may have been composed in Italy'.
Open question had no theories (schema requires 2-4).

question: Who wrote the Voynich manuscript, and is its text a real language?
evidence: Vellum radiocarbon dated 1404–1438; word frequencies follow Zipf's law; character sequences are more predictable than typical languages.
wouldSettle: A verified decipherment yielding coherent text, or documents identifying its maker and method.

theories.name: Cipher of a known language
theories.idea: Meaningful text hidden by a cipher, perhaps a verbose cipher; Bowern finds simple substitution and polyalphabetic ciphers do not fit its statistics.

theories.name: Natural or constructed language
theories.idea: Its statistics resemble natural language; an encoded natural language or invented language has been proposed (Bowern).

theories.name: Meaningless or hoax text
theories.idea: It may be glossolalia, fiction or a deliberate hoax; Duffy says vellum dating rules out a post-medieval forgery.
